prose.text: The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order: capability-drift before the default-features workspace nextest, then the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen, then the base-identity bindings close (no procedure is added). The chunk's own gates come first, all under `--workspace` (test-plan §11 run-scope rule): - a collection proof; - the two new test binaries; - a placement probe (the apply call is `main()`'s first statement); - the scope guard; - a log-content census (no preset value can reach a log call).

Absences and bindings, each with its reason: - No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent. - No dependency is added (`std` only), so `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not listed locally. CI's `supply-chain`   job runs them, and the operator CI read asserts it green. - `pulse-app/src/main.rs` and `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` are boot-smoke trigger paths, so the boot smoke   BINDS (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate). It takes the direct-binary variant, which is the two live legs below. Both   are `leg = 'operator'`: they open windows on the operator's display, so /implement fires each ONCE on the   operator's granted slot, and the wrap's light gate never re-runs them. `cargo xtask self-verify` is a Windows/WRY   headful harness and is not this chunk's witness. - RED-before-green: the RED leg was measured at P3 on the untouched base. The PRESET leg is the discriminating control: it   proves the preset is honoured, and that the lever, not some other change in this chunk, keeps the app up.
